comparator.name: Medicine
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official TER defines a compulsory 180-EC Bachelor of Medicine organized into Causes of Diseases, longitudinal Knowledge Development and Competency Development. Competency Development is delivered through one of four Learning Communities: Sustainable Care, Intramural Care, Innovative Healthcare or Global Healthcare. The medical-knowledge curriculum is common across the routes, and current official evidence does not establish one Learning Community as more representative or more general. Sustainable Care is therefore instantiated through the official-order tie-break because it is listed first in the TER. The selected coherent pathway preserves all 60 EC in each year and contains no minor or free-elective space within the 180-EC degree.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Medicine target offers four Learning Communities for the Competency Development components while retaining one common medical-knowledge curriculum. Current official evidence does not identify one community as the broad default or academically dominant route. Sustainable Care is therefore selected neutrally because it is listed first in the 2026-2027 TER, without reference to UCR fit.

exception.reason: The Groningen bachelor is the first professional phase of medical training and integrates broad biomedical and pathophysiological knowledge with longitudinal clinical reasoning, patient-centred problem-based learning, medical consultation, diagnosis and treatment decisions, communication with patients and professionals, supervised competency development, healthy-ageing and prevention work, scientific training, professional formation and recurring medical knowledge progression tests. UCR can build a strong biomedical-science curriculum and add psychology, population health and research methods, but it does not offer clinical medical education, supervised patient contact, medical consultation training, diagnostic and treatment practice, clinical placements, longitudinal physician competencies or a comprehensive medical progress-testing sequence. A 24-course UCR schedule would therefore be a defensible biomedical or health-sciences programme, but not a defensible closest match to Medicine.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026-2027 TER accounts for exactly 180 EC with no elective or minor space inside the degree. Year 1 contains 35 EC of six integrated Causes of Diseases modules, 4 EC of Knowledge Development and 21 EC of Competency Development. Year 2 contains 36 EC of six Causes of Diseases modules, 4 EC of Knowledge Development and 20 EC of Competency Development. Year 3 contains 26 EC of five Causes of Diseases modules, 4 EC of Knowledge Development and 30 EC of Competency Development, including advanced clinical reasoning and a Bachelor's Project. The official study guide explains that Causes of Diseases integrates basic and clinical disciplines around patient problems, while Competency Development follows longitudinal pathways in professional development, medical consultation, healthy ageing and scientific training.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine; HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology; HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology; HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry; HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory; HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics; HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy; HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology; HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity; and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide substantial biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar add population health, methods, patient-context and research perspectives. The workbook contains no clinical-medicine course sequence, supervised patient-contact or clinical-placement component, medical consultation and examination skills, systematic diagnosis and treatment training, clinical reasoning under medical supervision, longitudinal physician-professional competency programme or whole-programme medical progress testing. Adjacent psychology, cognition, ethics, law, sociology and data courses can broaden health study but cannot replace these defining professional and clinical requirements. The available courses therefore cannot form a defensible 24-course Medicine programme.
